column1: # label_typo_review answers read locally, 2026-08-04. Batch 1 of the 143.
# THE DOMINANT FINDING. A large family of these labels was produced by a
# romanizer that collapsed a doubled vowel into a macron ACROSS A MORPHEME
# BOUNDARY: 飯玉 いいたま became "ītama", 飯塚 "īzuka", 幣石 へいいし "Heīshi",
# 二荒 ふたあら "Futāra", 堀出 ほりいで "Horīde". 飯 is い + the next morpheme's
# い — not a long vowel — so the correct forms are Iitama, Iizuka, Heiishi,
# Futaara, Horiide. Eleven of them also came out with a LOWERCASE initial
# ("ītama Shrine"), which is wrong under any romanization policy and is the
# clearest signal that no human wrote these.
# Only unambiguous cases are answered here. Left pending on purpose:
#   * style-only differences (Oomi/Ōmi/Omi, Kounomine/Kōnomine) — that is a
#     romanization-policy question for Emma, not a typo;
#   * cases where the KANA and the LABEL disagree about the READING itself
#     (石上 いしがみ vs Isonokami, 四本木 しほんぎ vs Yomotogi, 鵜鳥 うねどり vs
#     Unotori) — either could be right and the item decides, not a rule;
#   * descriptive labels that may be deliberate (合氣神社 "Iwama Dōjō",
#     海底神社 "Underwater Shrine", 合祀：大津神社 "Co-Enshrinement of Hyōzu
#     Shrine"), since a weird thing on this data is usually signal.
# ─── LABEL_TYPO: a description leaked into the label ───
# ─── PREFIX_OK: the label carries a place prefix the bare-name kana cannot ───
